definition: The principle that good representations compress the input while preserving task-relevant information, framing learning as a tradeoff between compression and prediction.
details: The principle that good representations compress the input while preserving task-relevant information, framing learning as a tradeoff between compression and prediction. Contested as a literal account of deep learning dynamics, but influential as a design and analysis lens.

explainer.lead: The information bottleneck frames learning as a tradeoff: a good representation compresses the input while keeping what is relevant to the task. It matters as a design and analysis lens for what representations should keep and discard.

tiers.eli5: Think of summarizing a long report for a specific meeting: you cut most of the text but must keep the points that matter for that meeting. The bottleneck idea says good representations do exactly that.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it as a principle for shaping representations—squeezing out input detail while preserving task-relevant signal. Its use as a literal explanation of deep learning dynamics is contested, so treat it as a lens rather than a guaranteed mechanism.
tiers.paperLevel: Good representations compress the input while preserving task-relevant information, expressed as a tradeoff between compression and prediction. It is influential as a design and analysis lens but contested as a literal account of deep learning dynamics.

explainer.example: A representation that keeps only features predictive of the label while discarding nuisance variation follows the bottleneck tradeoff: high compression, high preserved task-relevant information.
